content:
The Acid Rain Program didn’t use one emissions mechanism for both sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.

Under Title IV, the sulfur dioxide system used an aggregate cap and tradable allowances. Each allowance represented permission to emit one ton within that permitted total.

That system expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.

Nitrogen oxides regulation for certain coal-fired units followed a different track. It began in 1996 and was rate-based, with no cap or allowance trading.

The program addressed both pollutants, but through distinct mechanisms and timelines.
